items.message: This change implements GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an open change request force-pushes to that branch rather than opening a second pull request. The implementation covers the full surface: detection of an existing CR filtered to the `implement` verb, person-commit refusal before any write, leased force-push with the sha the check read, draft-state restoration on a red second attempt, and the credential-in-error suppression that keeps git stderr out of public ticket comm…[truncated]
`getattr` guard for `mark_draft` is asymmetric with `mark_ready`.
`_existing_change_for` catches `RuntimeError` and `OSError` but not every failure `changes_for` might raise.

Real-git tests rely on `_an_attempt_already_on_the_remote` using `file://` URLs, which means the credential-leakage test uses a fake secret that `file:///nowhere/s3cr3t-token-value/repo.git` embeds in a path rather than a URL userinfo field.

This change adds an update path for `/implement` when a change request already exists for a ticket: it force-pushes to the existing branch with a lease on the sha it read, refuses if a person's commit is present or the branch is unreadable, and puts the CR back into draft if tests did not pass. The performance lens has nothing to report. The new code runs once per workflow invocation — one `changes_for` call, one `fetch_branch`, one push — none of which is inside a loop over user-scaling data. T…[truncated]

This change adds a force-push update path for a second `/implement` run on a ticket that already has an open pull request. The security-relevant surface is: the `TargetRefused` prose posted to public ticket comments, the git stderr redaction that keeps credentials out of those comments, and the person-commit detection that prevents silent overwriting of human work. I checked the credential-leak path carefully: both adapters catch `RuntimeError` from the push, print git's text to stdout (which th…[truncated]
Credential-redaction relies on a stdout wrapper that is not enforced at this call site.
Same stdout-redaction assumption as github.py — credential in git stderr reaches print() if the wrapper is absent.

This change introduces GATE-REVIEW-8: a second `/implement` on a ticket with an existing open change request now force-pushes to that branch rather than opening a new one. The new test file `test_update_existing_change.py` is substantial and deliberately structured — it tests the stub-level routing (which path is taken, which sha is passed, which verb's CR is targeted) and then separately tests the real-adapter properties over genuine git (building over HEAD, the lease, credential-in-URL scrubbi…[truncated]
No test covers `_existing_change_for` printing its warning and falling through when `changes_for` raises.

The two-CR test (`test_two_open_crs_uses_the_one_resolved_through`) asserts the comment names `newer.url` but does not assert the reason `update_change` is called is the newest — it asserts `scm.updated[0]["change"].number == 42`, which is also `newer`'s number. The assertion is correct but relies on both objects having the same value (42 and 42). `newer` is defined with `number=42` and `_EXISTING_CR` also has `number=42`.
No test asserts the `changes_for` result is filtered to `implement` branches when both `changes_for` and `update_change` are absent from the adapter.
